facts.raw_span: painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
without systemic symptoms
glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis with ipsilateral hydrocele
swelling persisted
bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement measuring 15×12 mm on the right and 27×18 mm on the left
these nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
intense uptake (SUVmax 25.5) in the right testis
no uptake in the adrenal glands
normal electrolytes, blood count, iron studies, protein electrophoresis, glucose, renal and liver function, thyroid profile, LDH, and β2-microglobulin
negative for active HCV and EBV (positive for past EBV)

concepts.why: The patient's painless testicular swelling, enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis, and intense uptake on PET/CT are consistent with testicular lymphoma.
The patient's testicular swelling, adrenal enlargement, and intense uptake on PET/CT could be explained by metastatic testicular cancer.
The patient's painless testicular swelling and intense uptake on PET/CT are consistent with primary testicular seminoma.
The patient's testicular swelling and intense uptake on PET/CT could be explained by a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor.
The patient's bilateral adrenal enlargement could be explained by adrenal incidentalomas.
it explains the absence of uptake in the adrenal glands on the 18 FDG PET/CT scan

rationales.F01: Painless testicular swelling is a common presentation of testicular cancer.
rationales.F05: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the testis is a strong indicator of testicular cancer.
rationales.F07: Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement is more likely to be an incidentaloma than metastatic disease.
rationales.F09: Intense uptake in the right testis on PET/CT is highly suggestive of testicular cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: intense uptake in the right testis and testicular ultrasound findings are consistent with primary testicular seminoma, while lack of systemic symptoms and specific laboratory findings argue against lymphoma or other aggressive processes
